outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the landscape of mathematical reasoning in AI, highlighting the gap between closed-source giants and open-source models. It defines the core objectives of the DeepSeekMath project, outlines the significance of the MATH benchmark, and previews the two main pillars of success: high-quality data curation and novel reinforcement learning.
subtopics: The Challenge of Structured Mathematical Reasoning
Current State of Open vs. Closed Source Models (GPT-4, Gemini vs. Open Alternatives)
Overview of Key Benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, and Formal Proofs
Project Goals: Bridging the Performance Gap with Efficient Architectures
Summary of Contributions: Scalable Pre-training and GRPO

outline.description: This chapter details the methodology for creating the DeepSeekMath Corpus. It explores the iterative data mining pipeline from Common Crawl, emphasizing how active learning and classification refine web data into a massive, multilingual mathematical resource while ensuring benchmark integrity.
subtopics: Limitations of Existing Math Corpora (Minerva, OpenWebMath, Proof-Pile)
The Iterative Mining Pipeline: From Seed Corpus to FastText Classifiers
Domain Identification and Manual Annotation Strategies
Decontamination Techniques: Preventing Benchmark Leakage via N-gram Filtering
Quantitative Validation: Comparing Token Counts and Downstream Performance Across Corpora

outline.description: Focuses on the creation and evaluation of the foundational model. This chapter analyzes why initializing from a code-specialized model is advantageous for math reasoning and presents empirical evidence comparing deep-seek-base against larger baselines like Minerva.
subtopics: Initialization Strategy: Why Start with DeepSeek-Coder?
Curriculum Design: Mixing Math Tokens with Code and Natural Language
**Key Finding:** Does Code Training Improve Reasoning? (Evidence from Two-Stage vs. Mixed Training)
**Counter-Intuitive Insight:** The Limited Utility of ArXiv Papers in Math Pre-training
Performance Evaluation: Chain-of-Thought Prompting on English and Chinese Benchmarks

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Instruction Alignment
outline.description: Describes the transition from a base model to an instruction-following agent. This chapter covers the construction of diverse SFT datasets involving Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), and tool-integrated reasoning formats.
subtopics: Dataset Construction: Curating Multi-Linguistic Problems (English & Chinese)
(CoT): Generating Step-by-Step Explanations
(PoT): Leveraging Python Execution for Verification
(ToRA): Integrating External Tools for Complex Calculations
(Training Protocol): Context Length Management and Hyperparameter Tuning
outline.title: Chapter 7
outline.description: Provides a unified theoretical lens to compare modern alignment techniques.
subtopics: Unified Paradigm Definition
